newsitem.title: GREECE: Upbeat construction spurs Greek bourse 1.68pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat construction spurs Greek bourse 1.68pct higher.

text.p: Greek shares were awakened at mid-session from their early lethargy by a bouyant construction sector which had a knock-on effect on the broader market. The benchmark index raced ahead 1.68 percent.
"With nearly half the construction sector closing at or near its upper daily volatility limit it is apparent there is a mispricing," said Dimitris Paparistidis, director at Kappa Securities.
"Investors are moved by sentiment when pricing construction stocks and are not yet decided between superior and inferior companies," he added.
Construction stocks have underperformed this year's rally. Paparistidis said construction stocks were out of vogue, attributing their recent weakness to concerns over liquidity problems in Atemke.
"Investors were spooked by Atemke's hardships, steering clear of all sector stocks," he said.
"But there are construction firms with sizeable orderbooks and good track records which justify a far higher market price," he added.
July CPI inflation eased to 5.4 percent from June's 5.5 percent, in line with market expectations.

"The market offers excellent buying opportunities around these levels and stocks will see higher demand from the latter half of August onwards as investors will focus on a number of events that will take place in September and will affect economic policy and corporate developments," said Paparistidis.

These include the prime minister's speach on economic policy at the Thessaloniki Trade Fair, the rights issues of flagship stocks such as National Bank and Intracom, decisions on large state supplies and the selection of the host city for the 2004 Olympics, he added.
The Athens general index climbed 1.68 percent or 26.55 points to 1,611.46 from Tuesday's 1,584.91.
Construction jumped 6.49 percent, followed by industrials, up 1.80 percent, and banks, up 1.65 percent.
Turnover picked up to 11.6 billion drachmas on volume of 3.5 million shares, boosted by block trading in cigarette manufacturer Papastratos and a number of second-tier issues.
Advancers beat decliners 140 to 67 with 20 shares unchanged on 227 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.4-$10.8. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,120-1,150 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,052-1,112 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock firmed 25 drachmas to 6,295.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 655.94-697.81 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $71.16-$73.91. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,563-3,787 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $10.85 bid/no offer. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 236-268 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
